samples.rationale: The pinned PUT operation creates or updates a CapacityReservation with a required reserved SKU and capacity. Existing machine-capacity-profile describes reusable sizing, not a lifecycle-managed reservation of provider capacity, so this is a provisional extension.

The pinned REST path creates or updates an independently addressed VirtualRouter resource. No current concept or Azure projection represents a managed routing resource, so this is a provisional extension without asserting any unproven attachments.

Although exposed through PUT, the pinned operation says it performs a VIP swap and its SwapResource body selects the target slot. This is an imperative cloud-service operation rather than an omitted declarative infrastructure resource or configuration concept.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates an addressable RestorePointCollection and permits later tag updates. The current storage and image concepts do not model a collection boundary for compute restore points, so it warrants a provisional extension.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates a DdosProtectionPlan as its own resource. Existing network-security-policy-group is a traffic-filter rule container and does not cover managed DDoS protection, so this is a provisional extension.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates a distinct DiskAccess resource. It is neither data storage nor a compute-storage attachment, and the current crosswalk has no storage network-access boundary; the candidate name is provisional and asserts no relation beyond that resource boundary.

The pinned child PUT creates or updates an inbound NAT rule beneath a load balancer. A one-to-one frontend/backend port translation is not the current load-balancer listener plus backend-group balancing concept, so preserving this child configuration requires a provisional extension.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates a Snapshot as an independently managed resource. It is not directly attachable data-storage and is not an execution-environment machine image, so the existing concepts lose its point-in-time storage-copy identity.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates an independently addressed IpAllocation resource. Current IP network configuration covers subnet range, gateway, and allocation behavior but not a lifecycle-managed allocation object, so this is a provisional extension.

The pinned VM child endpoint creates or updates a persistent VirtualMachineRunCommand resource. One-time creation bootstrap data and TOSCA language-level operation structure do not cover this provider-managed runtime command child, so it is a provisional extension.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates an ApplicationSecurityGroup as its own resource. It groups application-facing network interfaces for use by security rules but is not itself the current rule-containing network-security policy group, so its identity needs a provisional extension.

The pinned endpoint creates an InterconnectBlock with pre-allocated SKU capacity, zones, and immutable hardware-placement constraints. No current compute, compute-group, or capacity-profile concept preserves this managed hardware-capacity block, so it is a provisional extension.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates a standalone NatGateway resource with SKU and zone placement. The current virtual-network and IP-segment concepts do not represent managed address-translation infrastructure, so this is a provisional extension.

The pinned child endpoint creates or updates a VirtualMachineScaleSetExtension with its own resource name and properties. It is not one-time bootstrap contextualization and is distinct from the scale set itself, so the child management-extension boundary is provisionally retained.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates a DSCP configuration for network interfaces as an independent resource. No current network or attachment concept preserves managed QoS marking configuration, so this is a provisional extension.

The pinned child endpoint creates an immutable-after-creation RestorePoint beneath a collection. Existing storage snapshot and machine-image semantics are absent from the current model and would not preserve this compute recovery-point child identity, so it is a provisional extension.

The pinned child PUT approves or rejects an addressable PrivateEndpointConnection beneath a private-link service. The current compute-network attachment models compute connectivity, not private-service connection state, so this is a provisional extension.

The pinned endpoint creates or updates a VMSS instance's VirtualMachineExtension as a distinct nested child resource. It is not one-time bootstrap contextualization and differs in ownership from the scale-set-level extension, so its instance-scoped boundary is provisionally retained.
